pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


Have you ever looked at a sign and wondered where it leads? Maybe you saw a sign for a beach but you were miles away from the water. Maybe you saw a sign for a restaurant but the building was empty. Signs point to something. They are not the thing itself. They are a promise of the thing.


The Old Testament law is a sign. It is a collection of rules about food and farming and clothing and disease. It is a collection of laws about sacrifices and festivals and priests. On the surface it looks like a rulebook. It looks like a list of dos and don'ts. But it is not. It is a sign. It is a symbol. It is a shadow. Every law was pointing to something. Every rule was revealing something. Every symbol was showing something.


This book is for the curious. It is for the spiritual seeker who senses there is more. It is for the person who wants to understand why ancient laws still matter today. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 ancient laws and symbols. We are going to decode them. We are going to see what they were really pointing to. And we are going to discover that every single one of them points to Jesus. And every single one of them reveals grace.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see the Old Testament law as a list of outdated rules. You will see it as a divine revelation. You will understand why the law was given. You will understand what it was pointing to. You will see the hidden pattern. And you will have a new lens to read the Bible. A lens that reveals Jesus in every law. And grace in every symbol.


How to Use This Guide

The Hook
Have you ever been the firstborn in your family? Maybe you are the oldest. Maybe you have an older sibling. In the ancient world, the firstborn was special. The firstborn got a double portion of the inheritance. The firstborn got the blessing. The firstborn got the authority. But God had a law about the firstborn. And it was a symbol. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal." - Exodus 13:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God told Moses to consecrate every firstborn male. The firstborn belonged to God. Why? Because God had saved the firstborn of Israel during the Passover. The firstborn was a reminder. It was a reminder of deliverance. It was a reminder of sacrifice. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters." - Romans 8:29


Jesus is the firstborn. He is the firstborn of all creation. He is the firstborn from the dead. He is the firstborn among many brothers and sisters. He is the fulfillment of the law of the firstborn. He is the one who receives the double portion. He is the one who receives the blessing. He is the one who receives the authority. And because we are in Him, we become part of the family. We become brothers and sisters. We share in His inheritance.


The Verdict
The law of the firstborn was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is that we are included.


The Resonance
Do you feel like you are not included? Do you feel like you are on the outside? Remember the firstborn. Remember Jesus. He makes you part of the family. You are not an outsider. You are a brother. You are a sister. You are included.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the firstborn. Thank you for making me part of the family. Thank you for including me. Thank you for sharing your inheritance with me. Help me to live like a son. Help me to live like a daughter. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever felt trapped? Maybe you felt trapped in a job. Maybe you felt trapped in a relationship. Maybe you felt trapped in a pattern of behavior. The Bible has a lot to say about slaves. It has a lot to say about freedom. And it has a lot to say about a specific law. A law that was a symbol.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free, without paying anything." - Exodus 21:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God gave a law about Hebrew slaves. A Hebrew slave could only serve for six years. In the seventh year, they had to go free. They did not have to pay to be free. They did not have to work for their freedom. It was a gift. It was a law of grace. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery." - Galatians 5:1


Jesus is the seventh year. He is the freedom. He is the release. He is the fulfillment of the law of the slave. He sets us free. Not because we earned it. Not because we deserve it. Because He is grace. He is freedom.


The Verdict
The law of the slave was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is freedom.


The Resonance
Are you trapped? Are you in bondage? Are you in slavery to something? Remember the law of the slave. Remember Jesus. He sets you free. You do not have to pay. You do not have to work. You just have to receive.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for setting me free. Thank you for the seventh year. Thank you for the release. Thank you for the grace. Help me to walk in freedom. Help me to stop returning to slavery. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever needed someone to rescue you? Maybe you needed someone to pay a debt. Maybe you needed someone to speak up for you. Maybe you needed someone to save you. The Bible has a law about a rescuer. It is called the kinsman redeemer. And it is a symbol.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"If one of your fellow Israelites becomes poor and sells some of their property, their nearest relative is to come and redeem what they have sold." - Leviticus 25:25 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The kinsman redeemer was a family member. If someone lost their land, a family member could buy it back. If someone sold themselves into slavery, a family member could buy them out. The redeemer had to be a relative. He had to be willing. He had to be able. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life handed down to you from your ancestors, but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect." - 1 Peter 1:18-19


Jesus is the kinsman redeemer. He is our relative. He became human. He became one of us. He is willing. He chose to redeem us. He is able. His blood is enough. He redeemed us. He bought us back. He paid the price. He is the fulfillment of the law.


The Verdict
The law of the kinsman redeemer was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is redemption.


The Resonance
Do you need to be redeemed? Do you need to be bought back? Do you need someone to pay your debt? Remember the kinsman redeemer. Remember Jesus. He is your relative. He is willing. He is able. He redeemed you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my kinsman redeemer. Thank you for becoming human. Thank you for becoming my relative. Thank you for paying the price. Thank you for redeeming me. Help me to live as one who has been bought back. Amen.
pages.title: Day 3: The Law of the Kinsman Redeemer

The Hook
The Year of Jubilee was a once in a lifetime event. It was a reset button. It was a fresh start. But it was also a symbol.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan." - Leviticus 25:10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Year of Jubilee was a year of freedom. Every fifty years, the Israelites were to proclaim liberty. Slaves were set free. Debts were cancelled. Land was returned. It was a year of grace. It was a year of restoration. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor." - Luke 4:18-19


Jesus is the Jubilee. He is the freedom. He is the release. He is the restoration. He is the fulfillment of the law. He proclaims good news to the poor. He proclaims freedom to the prisoners. He sets the oppressed free. He is the year of the Lord's favor.


The Verdict
The Year of Jubilee was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is freedom.


The Resonance
Do you need a fresh start? Do you need a reset? Do you need to be released? Remember the Jubilee. Remember Jesus. He is your freedom. He is your restoration. He is your fresh start.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Jubilee. Thank you for proclaiming freedom to me. Thank you for releasing me from bondage. Thank you for restoring me. Help me to walk in your freedom. Amen.
pages.title: Day 4: The Law of the Year of Jubilee

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever made a mistake that you thought would destroy you? Have you ever done something wrong and felt like there was no way out? The Bible has a law about a safe place. It is called the city of refuge. And it is a symbol.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'Select some towns to be your cities of refuge, to which a person who has killed someone accidentally may flee.'" - Numbers 35:10-11 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The cities of refuge were safe places. If someone killed a person by accident, they could flee to a city of refuge. The avenger of blood could not touch them there. They were safe. They were protected. They were given a second chance. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." - Romans 8:1


Jesus is the city of refuge. He is the safe place. He is the protection. He is the second chance. He is the fulfillment of the law. When we run to Him, we are safe. We are protected. We are not condemned.


The Verdict
The law of the cities of refuge was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is safety.


The Resonance
Do you need a safe place? Do you need protection? Do you need a second chance? Remember the cities of refuge. Remember Jesus. He is your safe place. He is your protection. He is your second chance.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my city of refuge. Thank you for being my safe place. Thank you for protecting me. Thank you for the second chance. Help me to run to you. Help me to stay in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 5: The Law of the Cities of Refuge

pages.body:
The Hook
The Sabbath was a day of rest. It was a day of ceasing. But it was also a symbol. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God." - Exodus 20:8-10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Sabbath was a gift. It was a gift of rest. It was a gift of time. The people were told to stop working. They were told to stop striving. They were told to rest. They were told to trust. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest." - Matthew 11:28


Jesus is the Sabbath. He is the rest. He is the ceasing. He is the fulfillment of the law. He says, "Come to me. I will give you rest." Not the rest of a day. The rest of a lifetime. Not the rest of a ceremony. The rest of a relationship.


The Verdict
The Sabbath was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is rest.


The Resonance
Are you tired? Are you weary? Remember the Sabbath. Remember Jesus. He is your rest. He is your peace. Come to Him.


The Prayer
Jesus, I am tired. I am weary. Thank you for being my rest. Thank you for being my Sabbath. Help me to stop striving. Help me to rest in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 6: The Law of the Sabbath

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Why did God care about a baking ingredient? Why did He tell the Israelites to remove all yeast from their homes? It seems like a small thing. It seems like a weird detail. But it is a symbol. It is a clue. It points to something deeper.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day that I brought your divisions out of Egypt." - Exodus 12:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


When the Israelites left Egypt, they had to leave quickly. They did not have time to let their bread rise. They baked unleavened bread. But God told them to keep celebrating this festival. For seven days every year, they were to remove all yeast from their homes. Yeast was a symbol of sin. It spreads. It puffs up. It was a reminder to live a holy life. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore let us keep the Festival, not with the old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the bread of sincerity and truth." - 1 Corinthians 5:8


Paul applies this to Jesus. He says we are to remove the yeast of sin from our lives. We are to live with sincerity and truth. Jesus is the Bread of Life. He is the unleavened bread. He is without sin. If we want to live like Him, we must remove the yeast.


The Verdict
The law of unleavened bread was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is holiness.


The Resonance
What is the yeast in your life? What is the thing that puffs you up? What is the thing that spreads? God is asking you to remove it.


The Prayer
God, help me to remove the yeast from my life. Help me to stop tolerating the things that separate me from you. Give me a heart of sincerity and truth. Help me to live a holy life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 7: The Law of the Unleavened Bread

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever given someone your first paycheck? There is something special about the first. It is the best. It is the earliest. God asked the Israelites to give Him their firstfruits. He asked for the first. This is a symbol of resurrection.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God." - Exodus 23:19 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The firstfruits was an offering. It was the first sheaf of the harvest. The Israelites were told to bring it to God. It was a sign of trust. It showed they believed God would provide the rest. But it was also a symbol. The firstfruits was a promise that a greater harvest was coming.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep." - 1 Corinthians 15:20


Jesus is the firstfruits. He is the first to rise from the dead. His resurrection is a promise that we too will rise. If the firstfruits is raised, the rest will be raised too. This is the hope of the Christian faith.


The Verdict
The law of the firstfruits was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is resurrection.


The Resonance
Do you believe in the resurrection? If He rose, then the rest will rise. The firstfruits is a promise. The harvest is coming.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for rising from the dead. Thank you for being the firstfruits. Thank you for the promise that we will rise too. Thank you for the hope of eternal life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: The Law of the Firstfruits

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a sermon about tithing? Maybe you felt guilty. Maybe you felt confused. Maybe you felt like the church just wanted your money. But the tithe is not about money. It is about trust. And it is a symbol.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"A tithe of everything from the land, whether grain from the soil or fruit from the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD." - Leviticus 27:30 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The tithe was ten percent. The Israelites were told to give ten percent of their crops and their livestock to God. It was a sign of trust. It was a sign of gratitude. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Honor the LORD with your wealth, with the firstfruits of all your crops; then your barns will be filled to overflowing, and your vats will brim over with new wine." - Proverbs 3:9-10


Jesus is the tithe. He is the ten percent. He is the firstfruits. He is the fulfillment of the law. He gave everything. He gave one hundred percent. And because He gave everything, we can give generously. We can trust God with our money.


The Verdict
The law of the tithe was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is generosity.


The Resonance
Do you trust God with your money? Do you trust Him with your resources? Remember the tithe. Remember Jesus. He gave everything for you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for giving everything for me. Thank you for being the tithe. Thank you for being the firstfruits. Help me to trust you with my money. Help me to be generous. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: The Law of the Tithe

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The Sabbath Year was a year of rest for the land. It was a year of trust. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"For six years you are to sow your fields and harvest the crops, but during the seventh year let the land lie unplowed and unused." - Exodus 23:10-11 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Sabbath Year was a year of rest. The people were told not to plant. They were told not to harvest. They were told to trust God to provide. It was a year of faith. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"So do not worry, saying, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' or 'What shall we wear?' For the pagans run after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them." - Matthew 6:31-32


Jesus is the Sabbath Year. He is the trust. He is the rest. He is the provision. He is the fulfillment of the law. He tells us not to worry. He tells us to trust. He tells us that the Father knows what we need.


The Verdict
The law of the Sabbath Year was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is provision.


The Resonance
Do you worry? Do you struggle to trust? Remember the Sabbath Year. Remember Jesus. He is your provision. He is your trust.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Sabbath Year. Thank you for providing for me. Thank you for teaching me to trust. Help me to stop worrying. Help me to trust in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 10: The Law of the Sabbath Year

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The clean and unclean laws were rules. They were rules about food. They were rules about touch. They were rules about disease. They were a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between living creatures that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten." - Leviticus 11:47 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The clean and unclean laws were a lesson. They were a lesson about holiness. They were a lesson about separation. They were a lesson about being set apart. The people were told not to eat certain animals. They were told not to touch certain things. They were told to be different from the nations around them. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The voice spoke to him a second time, 'Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.'" - Acts 10:15


Jesus is the clean and unclean. He is the transformation. He is the fulfillment of the law. He makes the unclean clean. He makes the impure pure. He makes the unholy holy. He does not just give a list of rules. He gives a new heart. He gives a new nature. He gives a new identity.


The Verdict
The law of clean and unclean was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is purity.


The Resonance
Do you feel unclean? Do you feel impure? Do you feel unholy? Remember the clean and unclean laws. Remember Jesus. He makes you clean. He makes you pure. He makes you holy.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for making me clean. Thank you for making me pure. Thank you for making me holy. Thank you for the new heart. Thank you for the new nature. Thank you for the new identity. Help me to live in that identity. Amen.
pages.title: Day 11: The Law of the Clean and Unclean

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The priest was the mediator. He was the go-between. He was the symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Have Aaron your brother brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, so they may serve me as priests." - Exodus 28:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The priest was the representative. He represented the people before God. He offered sacrifices. He made atonement. He interceded. He was the mediator. He was the go-between. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has ascended into heaven, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to the faith we profess." - Hebrews 4:14


Jesus is the priest. He is the mediator. He is the go-between. He is the fulfillment of the law. He represents us before God. He intercedes for us. He understands our weaknesses. He was tempted. He did not sin. He is the perfect high priest.


The Verdict
The law of the priesthood was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is access.


The Resonance
Do you need a mediator? Do you need someone to represent you? Remember the priest. Remember Jesus. He is your mediator. He is your representative. He is your intercessor.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my High Priest. Thank you for representing me before God. Thank you for interceding for me. Thank you for understanding my weaknesses. Help me to come boldly to the throne of grace. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: The Law of the Priesthood

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The sacrifices were the center of the Old Testament law. They were about blood. They were about fire. They were about atonement. They were a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"For the life of a creature is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for yourselves on the altar; it is the blood that makes atonement for one's life." - Leviticus 17:11 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The sacrifices were a gift. They were a gift of grace. They were a gift of atonement. The people would bring an animal. They would lay their hands on it. They would confess their sin. The animal would be killed. The blood would be shed. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"In fact, the law requires that nearly everything be cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness." - Hebrews 9:22


Jesus is the sacrifice. He is the blood. He is the atonement. He is the fulfillment of the law. His blood was shed. His life was given. His sacrifice was made. And because of Him, we are forgiven. We are cleansed. We are made new.


The Verdict
The law of the sacrifices was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is forgiveness.


The Resonance
Do you need forgiveness? Do you need atonement? Remember the sacrifices. Remember Jesus. His blood was shed for you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the sacrifice. Thank you for shedding your blood. Thank you for making atonement. Thank you for forgiving me. Help me to receive your forgiveness. Help me to live in your grace. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: The Law of the Sacrifices

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The Day of Atonement was the holiest day of the year. It was a day of fasting. It was a day of sacrifice. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month you must deny yourselves and not do any work—whether native-born or a foreigner residing among you—because on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you." - Leviticus 16:29-30 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Day of Atonement was a day of national cleansing. The high priest entered the Most Holy Place. He offered sacrifices for his own sin. He offered sacrifices for the sin of the people. The blood was sprinkled on the mercy seat. The people fasted. They waited. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"He did not enter by means of the blood of goats and calves; but he entered the Most Holy Place once for all by his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption." - Hebrews 9:12


Jesus is the Day of Atonement. He is the high priest. He is the sacrifice. He entered the Most Holy Place once for all. He obtained eternal redemption. The Day of Atonement was a rehearsal. The reality is the cross.


The Verdict
The law of the Day of Atonement was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is redemption.


The Resonance
Do you need atonement? Do you need cleansing? Remember the Day of Atonement. Remember Jesus. He made atonement for you. Once. For all.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Day of Atonement. Thank you for entering the Most Holy Place. Thank you for obtaining eternal redemption. Thank you for cleansing me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: The Law of the Day of Atonement

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
There were two goats on the Day of Atonement. One was sacrificed. The other was sent into the wilderness. The scapegoat carried the sins of the people away. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The goat will carry on itself all their sins to a remote place; and the man shall release it in the wilderness." - Leviticus 16:22 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The scapegoat was not sacrificed. It was sent away. The high priest would lay his hands on the head of the goat. He would confess the sins of the people. He would transfer the guilt onto the goat. Then the goat would be led into the wilderness. It would carry the sins away. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"We all, like sheep, have gone astray, each of us has turned to our own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all." - Isaiah 53:6


Jesus is the scapegoat. The sins of the world were laid on Him. He carried them away. He took them to the wilderness of the cross. He took them to the grave. He removed them from us. This is the fulfillment of the law.


The Verdict
The law of the scapegoat was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is removal.


The Resonance
Your sins are not just forgiven. They are removed. They are carried away. They are gone. You do not have to carry them anymore. Jesus took them.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my scapegoat. Thank you for carrying my sins away. Thank you for taking them to the grave. Thank you for removing them as far as the East is from the West. Help me to stop picking them back up. Amen.
pages.title: Day 15: The Law of the Scapegoat

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The red heifer was a strange ritual. It involved a red cow. It involved ashes. It involved water. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer without defect or blemish and that has never been under a yoke." - Numbers 19:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The red heifer was a sacrifice for cleansing. The red heifer was taken outside the camp. It was killed. It was burned. Its ashes were collected. They were mixed with water. They were sprinkled on the people. They were cleansed. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The high priest carries the blood of animals into the Most Holy Place as a sin offering, but the bodies are burned outside the camp. And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood." - Hebrews 13:11-12


Jesus is the red heifer. He suffered outside the city gate. He was burned. He was the ultimate cleansing. His blood cleanses us. His blood purifies us. He is the fulfillment of the law.


The Verdict
The law of the red heifer was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is cleansing.


The Resonance
Do you need cleansing? Do you feel dirty? Remember the red heifer. Remember Jesus. His blood cleanses you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the red heifer. Thank you for suffering outside the gate. Thank you for cleansing me. Cleanse my heart today. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
The bronze serpent is one of the strangest stories in the Bible. The people were dying. They were bitten by snakes. God told Moses to make a bronze snake. He told him to put it on a pole. Whoever looked at it would live. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"So Moses made a bronze snake and put it up on a pole. Then when anyone was bitten by a snake and looked at the bronze snake, they lived." - Numbers 21:9 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The people of Israel were in the wilderness. They were complaining. They were sinning. God sent fiery serpents to bite them. Many died. The people cried out for mercy. God told Moses to make a bronze serpent. He told him to put it on a pole. Whoever looked at it would live. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him." - John 3:14-15


Jesus is the bronze serpent. He was lifted up on a cross. He was raised up on a pole. Whoever looks at Him will live. Whoever believes in Him will have eternal life. It is not about your effort. It is about looking. It is about trusting. It is about believing.


The Verdict
The law of the bronze serpent was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is life.


The Resonance
Are you dying? Are you dying from sin? Are you dying from shame? Look at Jesus. He was lifted up for you. Look at Him and live.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being lifted up for me. Thank you for being raised on a cross. Thank you for the promise that whoever looks at you will live. I am looking at you. I am trusting in you. I am believing in you. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
The cities of refuge were safe places. They were places of protection. They were a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'Select some towns to be your cities of refuge, to which a person who has killed someone accidentally may flee.'" - Numbers 35:10-11 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The cities of refuge were safe places. If someone killed a person by accident, they could flee to a city of refuge. The avenger of blood could not touch them there. They were safe. They were protected. They were given a second chance. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." - Romans 8:1


Jesus is the city of refuge. He is the safe place. He is the protection. He is the second chance. He is the fulfillment of the law. When we run to Him, we are safe. We are protected. We are not condemned.


The Verdict
The law of the cities of refuge was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is safety.


The Resonance
Do you need a safe place? Do you need protection? Do you need a second chance? Remember the cities of refuge. Remember Jesus. He is your safe place. He is your protection. He is your second chance.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my city of refuge. Thank you for being my safe place. Thank you for protecting me. Thank you for the second chance. Help me to run to you. Help me to stay in you. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
The Sabbath Year was a year of rest for the land. It was a year of trust. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"For six years you are to sow your fields and harvest the crops, but during the seventh year let the land lie unplowed and unused." - Exodus 23:10-11 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Sabbath Year was a year of rest. The people were told not to plant. They were told not to harvest. They were told to trust God to provide. It was a year of faith. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"So do not worry, saying, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' or 'What shall we wear?' For the pagans run after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them." - Matthew 6:31-32


Jesus is the Sabbath Year. He is the trust. He is the rest. He is the provision. He is the fulfillment of the law. He tells us not to worry. He tells us to trust. He tells us that the Father knows what we need.


The Verdict
The law of the Sabbath Year was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is provision.


The Resonance
Do you worry? Do you struggle to trust? Remember the Sabbath Year. Remember Jesus. He is your provision. He is your trust.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Sabbath Year. Thank you for providing for me. Thank you for teaching me to trust. Help me to stop worrying. Help me to trust in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 19: The Law of the Sabbath Year

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The Year of Jubilee was a once-in-fifty-years event. It was a reset button. It was a fresh start. But it was also a symbol.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan." - Leviticus 25:10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Year of Jubilee was a year of freedom. Every fifty years, the Israelites were to proclaim liberty. Slaves were set free. Debts were cancelled. Land was returned. It was a year of grace. It was a year of restoration. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor." - Luke 4:18-19


Jesus is the Jubilee. He is the freedom. He is the release. He is the restoration. He is the fulfillment of the law. He proclaims good news to the poor. He proclaims freedom to the prisoners. He sets the oppressed free.


The Verdict
The Year of Jubilee was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is freedom.


The Resonance
Do you need a fresh start? Do you need a reset? Do you need to be released? Remember the Jubilee. Remember Jesus. He is your freedom. He is your restoration. He is your fresh start.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Jubilee. Thank you for proclaiming freedom to me. Thank you for releasing me from bondage. Thank you for restoring me. Help me to walk in your freedom. Amen.
pages.title: Day 20: The Law of the Jubilee

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The firstborn was special. The firstborn got the blessing. The firstborn got the inheritance. But God had a law about the firstborn. And it was a symbol.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal." - Exodus 13:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God told Moses to consecrate every firstborn male. The firstborn belonged to God. Why? Because God had saved the firstborn of Israel during the Passover. The firstborn was a reminder. It was a reminder of deliverance. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters." - Romans 8:29


Jesus is the firstborn. He is the firstborn of all creation. He is the firstborn from the dead. He is the firstborn among many brothers and sisters. He is the fulfillment of the law. And because we are in Him, we become part of the family.


The Verdict
The law of the firstborn was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is inclusion.


The Resonance
Do you feel like you are not included? Remember the firstborn. Remember Jesus. He makes you part of the family.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the firstborn. Thank you for making me part of the family. Thank you for including me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: The Law of the Firstborn

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The law of the slave was a law of freedom. It was a law of release. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free, without paying anything." - Exodus 21:2 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God gave a law about Hebrew slaves. A Hebrew slave could only serve for six years. In the seventh year, they had to go free. They did not have to pay to be free. It was a gift. It was a law of grace. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery." - Galatians 5:1


Jesus is the seventh year. He is the freedom. He is the release. He is the fulfillment of the law. He sets us free. Not because we earned it. Not because we deserve it. Because He is grace.


The Verdict
The law of the slave was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is freedom.


The Resonance
Are you trapped? Are you in bondage? Remember the law of the slave. Remember Jesus. He sets you free.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for setting me free. Thank you for the seventh year. Thank you for the release. Help me to walk in freedom. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: The Law of the Slave

pages.body:
The Hook
The kinsman redeemer was a family member. He was a rescuer. He was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"If one of your fellow Israelites becomes poor and sells some of their property, their nearest relative is to come and redeem what they have sold." - Leviticus 25:25 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The kinsman redeemer was a family member. If someone lost their land, a family member could buy it back. If someone sold themselves into slavery, a family member could buy them out. The redeemer had to be a relative. He had to be willing. He had to be able. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life handed down to you from your ancestors, but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect." - 1 Peter 1:18-19


Jesus is the kinsman redeemer. He is our relative. He became human. He is willing. He chose to redeem us. He is able. His blood is enough. He redeemed us.


The Verdict
The law of the kinsman redeemer was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is redemption.


The Resonance
Do you need to be redeemed? Remember the kinsman redeemer. Remember Jesus. He is your relative. He is willing. He is able.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my kinsman redeemer. Thank you for becoming my relative. Thank you for paying the price. Thank you for redeeming me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: The Law of the Kinsman Redeemer

pages.body:
The Hook
The Sabbath was a day of rest. It was a day of ceasing. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God." - Exodus 20:8-10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Sabbath was a gift. It was a gift of rest. The people were told to stop working. They were told to rest. They were told to trust. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest." - Matthew 11:28


Jesus is the Sabbath. He is the rest. He is the ceasing. He is the fulfillment of the law. He says, "Come to me. I will give you rest."


The Verdict
The Sabbath was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is rest.


The Resonance
Are you tired? Are you weary? Remember the Sabbath. Remember Jesus. He is your rest.


The Prayer
Jesus, I am tired. I am weary. Thank you for being my rest. Help me to stop striving. Help me to rest in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: The Law of the Sabbath

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The law of unleavened bread was a law about yeast. It was a law about sin. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day that I brought your divisions out of Egypt." - Exodus 12:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


When the Israelites left Egypt, they had to leave quickly. They baked unleavened bread. God told them to keep celebrating this festival. For seven days every year, they were to remove all yeast from their homes. Yeast was a symbol of sin. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore let us keep the Festival, not with the old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the bread of sincerity and truth." - 1 Corinthians 5:8


Paul applies this to Jesus. He says we are to remove the yeast of sin from our lives. We are to live with sincerity and truth. Jesus is the Bread of Life. He is the unleavened bread.


The Verdict
The law of unleavened bread was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is holiness.


The Resonance
What is the yeast in your life? God is asking you to remove it.


The Prayer
God, help me to remove the yeast from my life. Give me a heart of sincerity and truth. Help me to live a holy life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: The Law of the Unleavened Bread

pages.body:
The Hook
The firstfruits was an offering. It was the first sheaf of the harvest. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God." - Exodus 23:19 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The firstfruits was an offering. The Israelites were told to bring it to God. It was a sign of trust. It was a sign of gratitude. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep." - 1 Corinthians 15:20


Jesus is the firstfruits. He is the first to rise from the dead. His resurrection is a promise that we too will rise.


The Verdict
The law of the firstfruits was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is resurrection.


The Resonance
Do you believe in the resurrection? If He rose, then the rest will rise.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for rising from the dead. Thank you for being the firstfruits. Thank you for the promise that we will rise too. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: The Law of the Firstfruits

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The tithe was ten percent. It was a sign of trust. It was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"A tithe of everything from the land, whether grain from the soil or fruit from the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD." - Leviticus 27:30 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The tithe was ten percent. The Israelites were told to give ten percent of their crops and their livestock to God. It was a sign of trust. It was a sign of gratitude. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Honor the LORD with your wealth, with the firstfruits of all your crops; then your barns will be filled to overflowing, and your vats will brim over with new wine." - Proverbs 3:9-10


Jesus is the tithe. He gave everything. He gave one hundred percent. And because He gave everything, we can give generously. We can trust God with our money.


The Verdict
The law of the tithe was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is generosity.


The Resonance
Do you trust God with your money? Remember the tithe. Remember Jesus. He gave everything for you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for giving everything for me. Help me to trust you with my money. Help me to be generous. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: The Law of the Tithe

pages.body:
The Hook
The clean and unclean laws were rules about food and touch and disease. They were a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between living creatures that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten." - Leviticus 11:47 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The clean and unclean laws were a lesson about holiness. The people were told not to eat certain animals. They were told not to touch certain things. They were told to be different from the nations around them. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The voice spoke to him a second time, 'Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.'" - Acts 10:15


Jesus is the clean and unclean. He is the transformation. He makes the unclean clean. He makes the impure pure. He makes the unholy holy.


The Verdict
The law of clean and unclean was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is purity.


The Resonance
Do you feel unclean? Remember the clean and unclean laws. Remember Jesus. He makes you clean.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for making me clean. Thank you for making me pure. Thank you for making me holy. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: The Law of the Clean and Unclean

pages.body:
The Hook
The priest was the mediator. He was the go-between. He was a symbol of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Have Aaron your brother brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, so they may serve me as priests." - Exodus 28:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The priest was the representative. He represented the people before God. He offered sacrifices. He made atonement. He interceded. It was a symbol. It pointed to something. It pointed to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has ascended into heaven, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to the faith we profess." - Hebrews 4:14


Jesus is the priest. He is the mediator. He is the go-between. He represents us before God. He intercedes for us. He understands our weaknesses.


The Verdict
The law of the priesthood was a symbol. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The symbol is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is access.


The Resonance
Do you need a mediator? Remember the priest. Remember Jesus. He is your mediator.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my High Priest. Thank you for representing me before God. Thank you for interceding for me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: The Law of the Priesthood

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
The law was a symbol. The rituals were a symbol. The festivals were a symbol. But the substance is Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The law is only a shadow of the good things that are coming—not the realities themselves." - Hebrews 10:1 (Written around 60 A.D.)


The law was a shadow. It was a shadow of the good things that are coming. It was a shadow of the realities themselves. It was a shadow of Jesus. The law could not make perfect. The sacrifices could not make perfect. They were shadows. They were pointing to something greater. They were pointing to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"These are a shadow of the things that were to come; the reality, however, is found in Christ." - Colossians 2:17


Jesus is the reality. He is the substance. He is the fulfillment of the shadow. He is the good thing that is coming. He is the perfect one. He is the one who makes perfect.


The Verdict
The law was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus. And the grace is reality.


The Resonance
You have the real thing. You have Jesus. You do not need to keep looking at shadows. You can live in the reality. You can live in the substance. You can live in Christ.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the reality. Thank you for being the substance. Thank you for being the fulfillment of the shadow. Help me to stop living in the shadow. Help me to live in the reality. Help me to live in you. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Substance Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 ancient laws and symbols. Now what? I challenge you to read the book of Galatians. It is 6 chapters. It is the perfect follow-up to this book. It will show you how the law was a guardian, a tutor, a shadow. And it will show you how Jesus is the substance. As you read, look for the shadows. Look for the substance. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The laws are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The laws point to a person. The laws point to Jesus. You can understand the laws and still miss the substance. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The laws are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.


Coming Next: Festivals of the Divine
If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. Festivals of the Divine takes a 30 day look at how ancient Israelite celebrations reveal the ultimate truth. It is for the seeker who wants to go further.
